result:
There is a particular kind of optimism in mending a thing.

Not the grand optimism of believing everything will turn out well. A smaller, sturdier kind: the belief that a loose button is worth sewing back on, that a bicycle chain can be coaxed into place, that the lamp might work if you change the bulb before declaring the room dark.

Repair asks us to pay attention. You have to find the crack, turn the object in your hands, learn how its parts fit together. Sometimes you discover that what looked broken was only disconnected. Sometimes you discover it cannot be fixed, and even then you know it more honestly than you did before.

I like that repair leaves evidence. A patched sleeve does not pretend it was never torn. It says: this was useful enough, or loved enough, to keep.
